description: Crack-Stix tops 6 driveway crack fillers for asphalt and Sikaflex Self-Leveling for concrete. Picks sorted by crack width, plus when to use backer rod.
dek: Crack-Stix tops 6 driveway crack fillers for asphalt and Sikaflex Self-Leveling for concrete.
intro: The best driveway crack filler for asphalt is Crack-Stix, a rubberized rope you melt into the crack with a torch, and the best for concrete is Sikaflex Self-Leveling Sealant. No single filler handles every job, though: the right one depends on what the driveway is made of and how wide and deep the crack is.

Cracks are where driveways start to fail. Water runs through them into the base, freezes, expands and pries the crack wider, and a few winters later a hairline is a pothole. Filling cracks is cheap, fast and does more for a driveway's life than any coat of sealer. Below are six picks matched to specific jobs, then how to size a crack, fill asphalt and concrete correctly, buy the right amount, and spot the cracks no filler will fix.
quickAnswer: Asphalt cracks of 1/4 to 1/2 inch: Crack-Stix melted in with a torch. Wide asphalt cracks and low spots: Latex-ite Trowel Patch. Concrete cracks and joints on level ground: Sikaflex Self-Leveling, or Quikrete Advanced Polymer Self-Leveling to save money. Visible concrete cracks on slopes or near the door: Sashco Slab. Chipped concrete edges: Quikrete Vinyl Concrete Patcher. Put backer rod in any crack deeper than about 1/2 inch.

sections.h: The 6 Best Driveway Crack Fillers in 2026 at a Glance

blocks.p: Match the filler to the pavement first, then to the crack width. Asphalt wants rubberized asphalt fillers that stay black and flexible. Concrete wants polyurethane or polymer sealants for cracks and cement patchers for chips. Get those two choices right and almost any product on this list will hold for years.

sections.h: The 6 Best Driveway Crack Fillers in 2026, Ranked

blocks.p: Picks are ranked on what each maker states on labels and data sheets (the crack widths each is rated for, cure and traffic times, flexibility) plus recurring themes in owner reports. Each wins a specific job, so read the award before the rank.

blocks.h3: Best Overall for Asphalt: Crack-Stix Permanent Blacktop Crack Filler

blocks.p: Crack-Stix is a rubberized asphalt rope. You press it into a clean crack and melt it with a handheld propane torch, and it flows against the crack walls and bonds. The result behaves much like the hot-pour material paving crews run from a kettle, which is why it holds up: asphalt cracks open in winter and close in summer, and a filler that stays rubbery keeps sealing through that movement. The rope comes in several sizes for different crack widths, so check the package range against your measurements. Owners commonly report it lasting through several winters where squeeze-bottle fillers shrank or pulled away. The cost is the process: a torch, steady hands, fire safety near dry grass and fuel cans, and more time per foot than pouring. For a driveway with a moderate number of 1/4 to 1/2 inch cracks, it is the most durable DIY result available.
**Pros:** Flexible, hot-pour-style seal; sized ropes for common widths; no mixing or bucket mess; can take traffic soon after it cools.
**Cons:** Needs a propane torch and careful handling; slower per foot than liquids; asphalt only.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Crack-Stix+Permanent+Blacktop+Crack+Filler&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best for Concrete Driveways: Sikaflex Self-Leveling Sealant

blocks.p: Sikaflex Self-Leveling is a one-part polyurethane made for horizontal concrete joints and cracks, which describes most of what goes wrong on a concrete driveway. Run a bead from a standard caulk gun and it flows into a smooth, level line on its own. Polyurethane stays elastic after it cures, which matters at control joints and at the seam where the driveway meets the garage slab or sidewalk, both of which move as temperatures swing. The data sheet calls for clean, sound, dry concrete and backer rod in deeper joints, so the sealant sits at the right depth and bonds only to the two sides. Because it self-levels, it runs downhill on a steep drive; use a non-sag polyurethane there. Full cure takes several days, and it is not made to fill wide, shallow spalls. For straight cracks and joints on a level slab, it is the most dependable concrete choice here.
**Pros:** Elastic polyurethane for moving joints; levels itself; standard cartridge; gray blends with most concrete.
**Cons:** Needs backer rod in deep cracks; slow full cure; runs on slopes.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Sikaflex+Self-Leveling+Sealant&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best Budget Concrete Filler: Quikrete Advanced Polymer Self-Leveling Sealant

blocks.p: Quikrete's Advanced Polymer Self-Leveling Sealant does the Sikaflex job at a lower price per cartridge and with easier availability, since it is a common home-center item. It flows into horizontal cracks on its own and cures to a flexible gray line that blends with ordinary broom-finished concrete. It suits the typical concrete driveway problem: a handful of hairline to 1/4 inch cracks and a few joints that have lost their old caulk. Like any self-leveling sealant, it needs a clean, dry crack, and anything deeper than about 1/2 inch should get backer rod or sand first so you end with a shallow, flexible bead instead of a deep plug. It will not stay put on a slope or vertical edge. Owners often describe it as easy for first-timers, and for routine upkeep on a level slab it does the job without paying for a premium brand.
**Pros:** Widely sold; self-levels in flat cracks; flexible once cured; budget-friendly.
**Cons:** Not for slopes or vertical faces; deep cracks still need backer rod or sand.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Quikrete+Advanced+Polymer+Self-Leveling+Sealant&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best for Wide Asphalt Cracks: Latex-ite Trowel Patch

blocks.p: Wide asphalt cracks defeat pourable fillers, which sink out of sight, and rope fillers top out at certain widths. Latex-ite Trowel Patch covers that gap. It is a thick, ready-to-use asphalt patching compound you push into wide cracks and shallow low spots with a putty knife or trowel, then smooth flush. Its heavy body stays where you put it on edges and gentle slopes where liquids would run. The label sets out cleaning, layer thickness and cure time, and following it matters: thick fills cure slowly, especially in cool weather, so build deep spots in layers. It is less flexible than a melted rope, so it suits wide cracks that are fairly stable rather than ones that open and close a lot. Once cured, most asphalt sealers go over it. For a mix of wide cracks and edge damage on blacktop, it is the practical pick.
**Pros:** Trowel-grade body stays put; ready to use; handles wide cracks and low spots; water cleanup while wet.
**Cons:** Slow cure in thick layers; less flexible than hot rope; asphalt only.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Latex-ite+Trowel+Patch&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best Concrete-Look Finish: Sashco Slab Concrete Crack Repair

blocks.p: Most concrete crack fillers leave a smooth, shiny line that looks like caulk. Sashco Slab is made to avoid that. It cures with a textured, sanded finish meant to blend with the concrete surface, which makes it a favorite for front walks, the apron at the top of a driveway and other cracks you see every day. It is formulated to stay highly flexible, so it follows cracks that move with temperature, and it is non-sag, so it works on slopes, steps and crack sides where self-leveling sealants would run. It cleans up with water while wet. The gray blends with most slabs but will not match every one exactly, and it looks best when the crack has been cleaned out first. It costs more per ounce than basic fillers, so use it where appearance counts rather than along long runs of joints.
**Pros:** Textured finish blends with concrete; very flexible; non-sag on slopes and edges; water cleanup.
**Cons:** Cartridge size limits big jobs; color match is close, not exact; higher cost per ounce.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Sashco+Slab+Concrete+Crack+Repair&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best for Chips and Spalls: Quikrete Vinyl Concrete Patcher

blocks.p: Not every concrete problem is a crack. Edges chipped by a snowplow, shallow spalls where the surface flaked, and wide gouges that do not move need a patching compound, not a sealant. Quikrete Vinyl Concrete Patcher is a polymer-modified cement you mix with water and trowel into the damage. The polymer helps it bond to old concrete and lets you feather it thin at the edges so the repair blends in. It cures hard like concrete, which is exactly right for a chipped edge and exactly wrong for a crack that opens and closes. Use it to rebuild missing material, and use a flexible sealant such as the Sikaflex or Quikrete self-leveling picks for active cracks and joints. Mix small batches, since you have to work it before it starts to set.
**Pros:** Rebuilds chipped edges and shallow spalls; feathers thin; mix only what you need; cures hard and paintable.
**Cons:** Rigid, so not for moving cracks; needs mixing and timing; concrete only.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Quikrete+Vinyl+Concrete+Patcher&tag=sktiger-20)

sections.h: How Wide Is Your Crack, and Which Filler Does It Need?

blocks.p: Crack width is the one number that decides which filler works. Walk the driveway with a tape measure and note the widest point of each crack, and whether it is a single line or part of a web.

blocks.p: Push a screwdriver into the crack. If it sinks more than about 1/2 inch, fill the bottom with backer rod, a closed-cell foam cord sold in rolls, or clean sand before the sealant goes in. Filling a deep crack entirely with sealant wastes product and makes a thick plug that flexes poorly.

blocks.h3: Check that both sides are level

blocks.p: In concrete, a crack where one side has dropped or lifted points to settling or heaving, and filling it will not fix the trip hazard. In asphalt, soft, crumbling crack edges often mean the base is failing.

sections.h: What Is the Best Asphalt Crack Filler for a Driveway?

blocks.p: For most asphalt driveways, a hot-applied rope filler such as Crack-Stix is the best choice, because it stays flexible as asphalt cracks open and close with the seasons. Asphalt is a flexible pavement; it bends a little under load and moves with temperature. Asphalt fillers are rubberized emulsions or hot-applied rubberized asphalt that bond to the binder, stay elastic and cure black so they blend in and take sealer.

Pre-formed strips of rubberized asphalt pressed in and melted with a torch. The most durable DIY seal on asphalt and the closest a homeowner gets to professional hot-pour. They take more time per foot and need careful torch use. Latex-ite Pli-Stix is a similar product.

Liquid rubberized emulsions in jugs or squeeze bottles. They are the fastest to apply and work in cracks from about 1/8 to 1/2 inch. They tend to shrink as they cure and may need a second pass, and they generally do not last as long as melted rope. For a few small cracks, pourable is fine.
Thick pastes like Latex-ite Trowel Patch handle wide cracks and shallow low spots. Cold patch asphalt fills potholes, which is a different job from crack sealing.

blocks.h3: Do not use concrete products on asphalt

blocks.p: A rigid cement patch in an asphalt crack pops out as the pavement flexes. Stay with asphalt products on blacktop.

sections.h: What Is the Best Concrete Crack Filler for Driveways?

blocks.p: For most concrete driveways, a self-leveling polyurethane such as Sikaflex Self-Leveling is the best crack filler, with a non-sag product for slopes and a cement patcher for chips. Concrete is rigid. It cracks as it shrinks while curing, when the ground below moves, or from freeze-thaw damage, and the cracks that matter most usually sit at control joints or where slabs meet.
Cartridge products like Sikaflex and Quikrete Advanced Polymer are the standard for cracks and joints on level ground. They flow into a smooth bead and cure flexible.
Products like Sashco Slab hold their shape on slopes, steps and vertical faces where self-leveling sealant would run.
Quikrete Vinyl Concrete Patcher rebuilds missing concrete at chipped edges and spalls. It is rigid, so keep it out of cracks that move.

blocks.h3: Do not use asphalt filler on concrete

blocks.p: Asphalt emulsion fillers bond poorly to concrete, and their black line stands out on a gray slab. After repairs, protect the whole slab with a penetrating sealer; see our [concrete driveway sealer rankings](/best-concrete-driveway-sealer-reviews/) and [how to seal a concrete driveway](/how-to-seal-a-concrete-driveway/).

sections.h: How Do You Fill Asphalt Driveway Cracks?

blocks.p: Pull weeds, moss and loose material with a crack weeder or screwdriver, then blow the crack clean with a leaf blower or compressed air. A wire brush loosens debris along the edges. Fillers do not bond to dirt, so this step decides how long the repair lasts. If moss keeps coming back, see [how to remove moss from an asphalt driveway](/how-to-remove-moss-from-asphalt-driveway/).
Wait at least a day after rain, longer in shade. Trapped moisture keeps fillers from bonding.
For cracks deeper than about 1/2 inch, add backer rod or clean sand to within roughly 1/2 inch of the surface.

ul: **Rope:** press it into the crack, then move the torch slowly along it until it melts and flows. Keep the flame moving so you do not scorch the surrounding asphalt.
**Pourable:** run the nozzle along the crack, fill slightly below the surface, and add a second pass if it shrinks.
**Trowel patch:** press it in firmly and smooth it flush.

blocks.p: Follow the label's cure time; many products ask for a day or more before sealer goes over the top. Fill cracks a few days before your sealing job. Then see [how to seal a driveway](/how-to-seal-a-driveway/) and pick a topcoat from our [asphalt driveway sealer rankings](/best-asphalt-driveway-sealer-reviews/).
Keep a fire extinguisher or a charged hose within reach, move vehicles and fuel cans well away, avoid dry grass or mulch on windy days, and follow the torch maker's directions.

sections.h: How Do You Fill Concrete Driveway Cracks?

blocks.p: Remove old caulk, weeds and loose concrete with a wire brush and shop vacuum. For narrow cracks with ragged edges, some manufacturers suggest widening them slightly with a grinder or chisel so the sealant has clean, solid walls to grip.

blocks.h3: Set the depth with backer rod

blocks.p: Let the concrete dry fully. In deeper cracks and joints, push in backer rod slightly wider than the crack so it fits snugly, sitting about 1/4 to 1/2 inch below the surface. The rod sets the sealant depth and stops it bonding to the bottom of the crack, so the bead can stretch freely as the crack moves.

Use a self-leveling sealant on level ground and a non-sag product on slopes. Fill to just below the surface; self-leveling products settle into a smooth bead on their own. Tape the edges for a crisp line if you like. Keep traffic off for the time on the label, and keep the area dry until the sealant has skinned over.
For chipped edges and flaked areas, remove loose material, dampen the area if the patcher label calls for it, and trowel the patch in, feathering the edges.

blocks.h3: What seals the crack between an asphalt driveway and a concrete sidewalk?

blocks.p: That seam moves, and the two materials want different chemistry. Use a flexible polyurethane or hybrid sealant rated for both concrete and asphalt, with backer rod underneath, rather than an asphalt filler or a rigid cement patch.

sections.h: How Much Crack Filler Do You Need?

blocks.p: Most people underestimate how much product a crack swallows. A 10.1-ounce caulk cartridge holds roughly 18 cubic inches.

blocks.h3: Why backer rod pays for itself

blocks.p: Without it, a deep crack can eat a whole cartridge in a few feet. With it, the sealant stays a shallow bead that uses less product and flexes better.
Check the package for the maker's coverage in linear feet at a given width, then add 20 to 30 percent for uneven widths, waste and a second pass.

Running out halfway along a crack leaves a seam in the repair. Most fillers keep reasonably well sealed in a cool, dry place for next year's touch-ups. For the bigger budget picture, see [how much it costs to seal a driveway](/how-much-does-it-cost-to-seal-a-driveway/).

sections.h: When Is the Best Time to Fill Driveway Cracks?

blocks.p: Mild spring or fall days are best. Most liquid and cartridge fillers list a minimum application temperature, commonly around 40 to 50 degrees F, and want a dry forecast for at least the first day. Check your product's label.

Asphalt and concrete shrink in cold weather, so cracks are at their widest. Filling them then puts the filler in compression in summer instead of stretching it thin in winter, which is easier on the bond. Filling in midsummer heat, when cracks are narrowest, can leave the filler overstretched by January.

If you are sealing the whole driveway, fill cracks a few days to a week ahead, following the filler's cure time. Our guides on [what temperature to seal a driveway](/what-temperature-to-seal-driveway/), the [best time to seal a driveway](/best-time-to-seal-driveway/) and [how often to seal your driveway](/how-often-should-you-seal-your-driveway/) help schedule both jobs.
Walk the driveway each fall and fill anything new, even in years you do not seal. It stops most cracks before winter can widen them.

sections.h: When Is a Crack a Sign of Something Bigger?

blocks.p: A pattern of connected cracks that looks like reptile skin usually means the base under the asphalt has failed or is saturated. Filling the individual cracks will not hold. The fix is to cut out the area and patch with new asphalt, usually a contractor job.

Cracks and crumbling along the sides of an asphalt driveway often come from missing support where soil has washed away or tires run off the edge. Filling helps, but building up soil or adding edging fixes the cause.

Cracks where one side sits higher than the other point to settling or heaving. Filling seals out water but does not fix the trip hazard; slab lifting or replacement may be needed. Cracks that widen year after year can also point to drainage problems or tree roots.

If more than about a quarter of the driveway shows these failures, get quotes on patching or resurfacing before spending on fillers and sealer. Our page on [sealing asphalt pros and cons](/sealing-asphalt-driveway-pros-and-cons/) covers when maintenance still pays. If you are shopping in person, our [Home Depot](/driveway-sealer-home-depot/) and [Menards](/driveway-sealer-menards/) guides cover what to put in the cart alongside the filler.

mistakes: Filling a dirty or damp crack

Fillers bond to clean, dry pavement, not to dust, moss or moisture. Skipping the cleanout is the most common reason repairs pop out within a season. Pull weeds, brush the edges, blow the crack clean, and wait at least a day after rain before you fill.
Pouring sealant into a deep crack with no backer

A deep crack can swallow a whole cartridge in a few feet, and a thick plug of sealant flexes poorly. Use foam backer rod or clean sand to bring the bottom up to within about 1/2 inch of the surface, then lay a shallow, even bead.
Using a rigid patch in a moving crack

Cement-based patchers are right for chipped edges but crack again in joints or cracks that open and close with temperature. Use a flexible polyurethane or polymer sealant for active cracks and keep patching compound for spalls and missing material.

Asphalt emulsion fillers bond poorly to concrete and leave a black line that stands out. Use a concrete sealant on concrete, an asphalt filler on asphalt, and a flexible sealant rated for both at the seam where they meet.

Putting sealer over crack filler before it cures can trap moisture and leave soft spots, dips or cracks in the topcoat. Read the filler's cure time and fill cracks a few days to a week before your sealing day.
bottomLine: For most asphalt driveways, Crack-Stix melted into clean, dry cracks gives the most durable result, with Latex-ite Trowel Patch for anything too wide for rope. For concrete, Sikaflex Self-Leveling is the dependable choice for cracks and joints, Quikrete Advanced Polymer is the budget alternative, Sashco Slab is the pick where looks and slopes matter, and Quikrete Vinyl Concrete Patcher rebuilds chipped edges. Whatever you buy, prep decides the outcome: clean, dry cracks, backer rod in anything deep, and full cure before sealing. Walk the driveway every fall and fill what is new.

faqs.q: What is the best driveway crack filler?
faqs.a: For asphalt, Crack-Stix melted in with a torch gives the most durable seal on typical 1/4 to 1/2 inch cracks, with Latex-ite Trowel Patch for wider ones. For concrete, Sikaflex Self-Leveling Sealant is the dependable pick for cracks and joints on level ground, and Quikrete Advanced Polymer is the budget alternative. Match the product to your surface and crack width.

faqs.q: What is the best asphalt crack filler for a driveway?
faqs.a: A hot-applied rubberized rope such as Crack-Stix. It melts into the crack, bonds to the walls and stays flexible as asphalt moves with temperature, much like professional hot-pour. Pourable fillers are faster and fine for a few narrow cracks, but they shrink and need more touch-ups. Use a trowel patch for cracks too wide for rope.

faqs.q: Is rope crack filler better than pourable?
faqs.a: For asphalt, yes in most cases. Rope melted with a torch gives a tougher, more flexible seal that owners report lasting several winters. Pourable fillers are quicker and easier but tend to shrink and need a second pass or yearly touch-ups. For a few small cracks, pourable is fine; for a driveway you plan to keep, rope is worth the effort.

faqs.q: Should cracks be filled before sealing a driveway?
faqs.a: Yes. Sealer is too thin to bridge anything much wider than a hairline, and coating over open cracks leaves a path for water into the base. Clean and fill cracks first, let the filler cure for the time on its label, often a day or more, then seal the whole surface. Our guide to [how long driveway crack filler takes to dry](/how-long-does-driveway-crack-filler-take-to-dry/) gives the wait for each filler type.

faqs.q: How long does driveway crack filler last?
faqs.a: It depends on the type. Torch-melted rope fillers are often reported to last several years. Pourable emulsion fillers tend to need touch-ups every year or two as they shrink. Polyurethane sealants in concrete can last many years when applied with backer rod at the right depth. A yearly walk-around and quick touch-ups keep everything sealed.

faqs.q: What is backer rod and do I need it?
faqs.a: Backer rod is closed-cell foam cord sold in rolls by diameter. You need it in any crack deeper than about 1/2 inch. Push it in so it sits 1/4 to 1/2 inch below the surface. It saves sealant, keeps the bead shallow so it flexes better, and stops the sealant from bonding to the bottom of the crack.

faqs.q: What is the best product to patch large holes and cracks in a driveway?
faqs.a: On asphalt, use a trowel-grade patch such as Latex-ite Trowel Patch for wide cracks and shallow low spots, and cold patch asphalt tamped in layers for potholes. On concrete, use a polymer-modified cement patcher such as Quikrete Vinyl Concrete Patcher for chips and spalls. If damage covers large areas, get a paving or concrete quote.
